text: [BLOCKER] The 25 "de novo designed" therapeutics are concatenations of copied natural motifs; no generative design pipeline exists anywhere in the repository — Every sequence presented as an AlphaFold3 de novo design is a literal substring of a small pool of pre-existing sequences. I tiled all 25 drug sequences against 10 parent strings (minimum match 6 aa): 801/839 residues = 95.5% coverage (876 total residues minus the 37-character non-sequence at app.js:381). Exact-match provenance against downloaded UniProt reference sequences: (1) app.js:225 / app.js:133 GRPRTTSFAESCKPVQQPSAFGSMKVSRDKDG = human GSK3B (P49841) residues 3-34, verbatim -- i.e. the target protein's own N-terminal tail; (2) app.js:126 APMKEANIRGQGGLAYPGVRT = human BDNF (P23560) residues 19-39, verbatim (prodomain, not mature BDNF); (3) app.js:277 / app.js:129 KLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLM = human APP (P05067) residues 687-706 = Abeta(16-35), verbatim; (4) app.js:127/163/309/339 DEETGEFL = NFE2L2 (Q16236) residues 77-84, the Nrf2 ETGE Keap1-binding motif, verbatim; (5) app.js:173/371/130 CKCHGMSGSCSTKTCWWG... = 14/21 identity to WNT3A (P56704) 203-223 CKCHGLSGSCEVKTCWWSQPD, the Wnt-family PROSITE signature; (6) GGGGS / GGSGGS throughout = the standard G4S flexible linker, not a design output. EBI blastp of the flagship 49-mer "TrkB D5 binder" MCVCDRENPVEWVRACPTGKCEGLRGYTCRCEPGWKGPDCRERACPDCH (app.js:128, and its variants at app.js:143, 183, 205, 267, 287, 361) against UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot returns MEGF11 (E=2e-05), Tenascin, Tenascin-X, Teneurin-3, Notch3, Jagged-2, Slit2 -- a generic EGF-like cysteine repeat pastiche -- and ZERO hits to NTRK2 (TrkB). Same for the "alpha7 nAChR / TLR4" 41-mer (app.js:134/195/319): top hits MEGF11/Teneurin EGF-like, no CHRNA7, no TLR4. The "Trem2 agonist" 31-mer (app.js:299): no hit better than E=1.5, no TREM2. The "AChE clamper" 36-mer (app.js:131/153/247): no meaningful hit at all (best E=0.016 to a Pasteurella toxin, i.e. noise). Consequence: "De novo design" is a load-bearing technical term with a defined meaning: sequence and backbone generated by a model conditioned on a target, not previously present in nature. Nothing here meets that definition. A reader -- a collaborator, a grant reviewer, a licensing partner, or an investor -- would reasonably believe 25 novel molecules exist and were generated by a design campaign. What exists is a curated motif library reassembled by hand. Any downstream decision (synthesis order, IP filing, partnership, publication) built on that belief is built on nothing, and the misrepresentation is discoverable in ten minutes by anyone who BLASTs a single sequence.

text: Required fix for AIML-01: Delete the phrase "de novo" from README.md:1, 13, 22, 43-45, 131, index.html:6-7, 30, 39, 53, 65, 106, 265-266, 326, and the BRAIN_REGIONS_DATA field label at app.js:525. Replace with "motif concatenation concept sketch (not experimentally or computationally validated)." Add a provenance table to the README giving, for every sequence, the UniProt accession and residue range of each borrowed motif (P49841 3-34, P23560 19-39, P05067 687-706, Q16236 77-84, P56704 ~203-223, G4S linker). If actual de novo designs are wanted, run RFdiffusion (or BindCraft) against a real target structure, sequence-design with ProteinMPNN, filter with AF2/AF3, and commit the design PDBs, the per-design score table, the random seeds, and the filter thresholds to the repository.

tags: Machine learning for protein / peptide binder design (generative models, inverse folding, in-silico filtering)
text: Ground truth for AIML-01: A 2020-2026 de novo binder campaign has a defined, auditable shape: (a) backbone generation conditioned on the target epitope -- RFdiffusion (Watson et al., Nature 620:1089-1100, 2023) or hallucination/AF2-backprop as in BindCraft (Pacesa et al., Nature 646:483-492, 2025); (b) sequence design on that backbone -- ProteinMPNN (Dauparas et al., Science 378:49-56, 2022) or LigandMPNN for small-molecule/metal contexts; (c) in-silico filtering by AF2/AF3 re-prediction of the complex from single sequence, plus self-consistency RMSD between the AF2 re-prediction and the design model, plus Rosetta interface ddG and shape complementarity; (d) wet-lab screening. Every step emits artefacts: design PDBs, per-design score CSVs, seeds, filter thresholds. None of that exists here. Motif grafting onto a scaffold is a legitimate and respected technique -- it is called motif scaffolding, and RFdiffusion explicitly supports it -- but it is not de novo design and must be labelled as motif grafting with the source motif and its PDB/UniProt provenance cited.

text: [BLOCKER] Identical sequences are assigned to structurally unrelated targets: only 21 unique sequences back the "25 targeted therapeutics", and the same 41-mer is simultaneously an alpha7 nAChR agonist and a TLR4 antagonist — Across the 10 AF3 candidates and 25 drugs there are 35 sequence entries but only 26 distinct sequences; within the 25 drugs alone there are only 21 distinct sequences. Worse than the duplication is the target contradiction. The identical 41-mer SEAEFRLFRDVWANYCACYPGWLGCDERACPRCHGFWREVC is declared to bind "alpha7 nAChR Extracellular Domain (ECD) (Tyr188, Trp149, Tyr195)" at app.js:196 and "TLR4 / MD-2 Complex (Arg264, Lys341, Glu439)" at app.js:320 -- a pentameric Cys-loop ligand-gated ion channel ECD and a leucine-rich-repeat innate-immune co-receptor, sharing neither fold nor surface chemistry. The identical 31-mer CKCHGMSGSCSTKTCWWGBLCPFRRACPDCH is a "Frizzled-8 CRD activator" (app.js:174, extracellular) and a "BMEC Zonula Occludens-1 (ZO-1) & Occludin Complex" binder (app.js:372) -- ZO-1 is a cytoplasmic PDZ/SH3/GUK scaffold that an extracellular peptide can never reach. The identical 37-mer VRACPTGKCEGL... is a "TrkB Ig-like D5 Domain" binder (app.js:206) and an "EAAT2 / GLT-1 (Thr368, Lys490)" binder (app.js:362). Each duplicate is nonetheless assigned different fabricated numbers: app.js:198 gives dG=-16.5, Kd=1.8 nM, pLDDT=93.2 while app.js:322 gives dG=-15.7, Kd=3.8 nM, pLDDT=92.8 for byte-identical input. AF3 is deterministic for a fixed input and seed; the same sequence against the same target cannot yield two pLDDT values, and pLDDT is in any case a monomer confidence metric that does not depend on the binding partner at all. Consequence: This is the internal-consistency test that no fabricated dataset survives. It proves the numbers were written to look plausible per-row rather than computed, and it proves the sequences were not designed against the targets they are advertised against -- a sequence cannot be optimised for two unrelated surfaces at once and then be given two different affinities for the same fold. An expert scanning the 25-drug grid at index.html:341 sees 25 distinct "targeted" molecules; the underlying data contains 21, several pointing at biologically impossible compartments. Anyone who ordered synthesis on this basis would buy the same peptide three times under three different programme codes.

tags: Machine learning for protein / peptide binder design (generative models, inverse folding, in-silico filtering)
text: Ground truth for AIML-02: Target-conditioned design produces target-specific sequences by construction: RFdiffusion and BindCraft take the target structure (and usually hotspot residues) as input, so two different targets cannot yield the same output backbone or sequence except by coincidence vanishingly unlikely at 31-41 residues. Where a designer deliberately wants one molecule to hit two targets, that is a bispecific and it is reported as one entry with two measured affinities, not as two entries with two different affinities for the same molecule. And pLDDT (Jumper et al. 2021; Abramson et al., Nature 630:493-500, 2024) is a per-residue predicted-LDDT confidence of the model's own coordinates -- for interface confidence the field uses ipTM and interface PAE, which are complex-specific; conflating them, as this dataset does by attaching a single "AF3 pLDDT" to a binding claim, is itself a metric error.

text: [BLOCKER] The pLDDT curves, PAE heatmaps and 3D structures are closed-form functions of ASCII character codes, not AlphaFold3 output; the platform assigns pLDDT ~94 to a placeholder string that is not a sequence — Three independent proofs that no AlphaFold3 run ever occurred. (1) The pLDDT generator at app.js:791 is a sinusoid plus a character-code term, hard-clamped to [76, 98.6] at app.js:792-793 -- so no input can ever produce a low-confidence region, which is the single most important thing a pLDDT plot exists to show. I evaluated the function: the real 36-mer at app.js:153 gives mean 94.1 (min 89.1, max 99.0); a string of 24 glutamines gives mean 94.3; and the placeholder string at app.js:381, "His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate", which contains digits, hyphens and lowercase and is not a sequence at all, gives mean 94.1 (min 89.1, max 99.0) -- byte-for-byte the same confidence profile as the real peptide. (2) The PAE generator at app.js:850 is dominated by |i-j|, which is the signature of a single perfectly rigid domain; it structurally cannot express the inter-domain block pattern that PAE exists to reveal, so the 100-mer at app.js:125 with three tandem GGGGS linkers -- which would show large inter-block PAE in any real prediction -- renders as a clean diagonal. Its maximum value on the 45x45 grid is 44*0.4 + 3*0.3 = 18.5 A, yet index.html:397 labels the axis 0-30 A. (3) The "3D structure" at app.js:711-732 and app.js:973-991 is a helix whose radius is `6 + (charCode % 5) * 0.8` -- a Catmull-Rom tube through a parametric spiral, containing no phi/psi angles, no Ramachandran constraint, no van der Waals term, no chirality. Separately, the leaderboard pLDDT values at app.js:125-134 contradict the drug-record pLDDT values for the same sequences: the identical 36-mer is 92.8 (app.js:131), 94.8 (app.js:156) and 94.3 (app.js:250), and the on-screen chart computes a fourth value (94.1). Finally, README.md:111 and index.html:42 advertise a "Live AlphaFold Server Connection"; there is no network call in the codebase -- index.html:42 and index.html:363 are ordinary <a href> hyperlinks to alphafoldserver.com. Consequence: This is the cleanest disproof of the platform's central provenance claim. A pLDDT curve and a PAE matrix are the two artefacts a structural biologist looks at first to decide whether a prediction is trustworthy. Here they are decorative and cannot fail, so they will endorse anything -- including a placeholder that says "Linker-Peptide-Conjugate" -- at 94 confidence. A viewer who cannot read the source (the entire intended audience of a web platform) has no way to tell these apart from real AF3 output, because they are labelled "AlphaFold3 pLDDT Score" (app.js:802) and "Real Sequence-Driven" (index.html:371, README.md:108). This is not a modelling shortcut; it is synthetic data presented under the name of a specific published method.

text: Ground truth for AIML-03: AlphaFold3 (Abramson et al., Nature 630:493-500, 2024) computes pLDDT from a learned confidence head over the diffusion module's output coordinates and PAE from a pairwise head; both require an MSA (or the AF3 single-sequence path), a full inference pass, and a seed, and both are highly sequence-dependent -- disordered linkers, unstructured termini and free short peptides routinely score pLDDT in the 30-60 range, and inter-domain PAE for a flexible fusion routinely exceeds 20 A. A correct implementation submits the sequence to the AlphaFold Server or runs the open AF3 weights, then parses the returned confidence JSON/mmCIF. Any pLDDT that cannot go below 76 by construction is not pLDDT.

text: [CRITICAL] Three sequences contain the invalid residue letter B, one "sequence" is a placeholder string, and nine contain an odd number of cysteines -- none of these are submittable to AlphaFold3 or synthesizable — B is the IUPAC-IUB ambiguity code Asx (Asn or Asp); it is not an amino acid and cannot be synthesized, expressed, or modelled. It appears at the same position in three separate entries, which shows it propagated by copy-paste rather than being a one-off typo. The AlphaFold3 input specification states the protein sequence field is "the amino-acid sequence, specified as a string that uses the 1-letter standard amino acid codes" (google-deepmind/alphafold3, docs/input.md); B, J, O, U, X and Z are not standard codes and the AlphaFold Server rejects them. app.js:381 is not a sequence in any sense -- it is a note to self. Yet all four flow through the same path: openDrugModal sets currentActiveModalSequence (app.js:600), the modal displays the string as "2. Sequence Structure (FASTA Peptide / Bio-Conjugate Sequence)" (index.html/app.js:619-621), copyModalFasta puts it on the clipboard (app.js:662), and index.html:359 instructs the user to paste it into the AlphaFold Server. Separately, nine sequences carry an odd cysteine count (5 or 7), which guarantees at least one unpaired free thiol; several others carry 6-8 cysteines with no disulfide connectivity declared anywhere -- the 47-mer at app.js:143 and the 45-mer at app.js:215 each have 8 cysteines, admitting 105 distinct all-paired disulfide topologies, and the code never states which one is intended. Consequence: Every one of these entries is a dead end at the first real step. A user who follows the platform's own instructions and pastes the X4/A3 sequence into the AlphaFold Server gets a validation error, and the A4 entry gets one immediately. A peptide chemist who orders the 5-cysteine or 7-cysteine constructs receives an intractable mixture of disulfide isomers and scrambled dimers -- unpurifiable, uncharacterizable, and unusable for any binding assay -- which is precisely why cysteine content is one of the first things a real design pipeline controls. The presence of a raw to-do note in a field the UI presents as a validated FASTA sequence, alongside a fabricated 94-pLDDT confidence report for it (see AIML-03), shows the dataset received no validation pass of any kind.

text: Ground truth for AIML-04: Sequences must be validated against the 20 standard one-letter codes before any downstream use; a two-line regex (`/^[ACDEFGHIKLMNPQRSTVWY]+$/`) catches all four defects here. Modern design pipelines handle cysteine explicitly: ProteinMPNN (Dauparas et al., Science 378:49-56, 2022) exposes an omit-AAs flag and cysteine is routinely excluded from designable positions unless a disulfide is deliberately scaffolded; BindCraft's default filter set (settings_filters/default_filters.json in martinpacesa/BindCraft) additionally screens on surface hydrophobicity <= 0.35, interface unsatisfied H-bonds <= 4, shape complementarity >= 0.6 and Rosetta dG < 0 before a design is ever ordered. For disulfide-rich macrocyclic peptides the current method is RFpeptides (Rettie et al., "Accurate de novo design of high-affinity protein-binding macrocycles using deep learning", Nature Chemical Biology, 2025, PMID 40542165), which designs the cyclization chemistry explicitly rather than leaving loose thiols.

text: [CRITICAL] Copy-pasting motifs without understanding them produced four mechanistically inverted or impossible designs, including grafting the amyloid-beta nucleating core into an "anti-amyloid" drug — (a) KLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLM (app.js:277, app.js:129) is APP 687-706 = Abeta(16-35) verbatim: it contains both the KLVFF self-recognition element and the entire hydrophobic C-terminal segment, and is the most amyloidogenic contiguous stretch of Abeta. It is presented as an "Abeta Disruptor" (README.md:77) with "Fibril Blockade: 100%" (app.js:281). Adding this peptide to brain tissue seeds aggregation; it is the positive control in fibrillization assays, not the inhibitor. Note the contrast with the correct approach: short KLVFF-derived inhibitors work only when the recognition element is truncated to ~5 residues and N-methylated or beta-sheet-broken precisely so it cannot itself extend a fibril. (b) app.js:225 is human GSK3B residues 3-34 verbatim -- the kinase's own N-terminal pseudosubstrate tail -- offered as an exogenous ligand for the GSK-3beta ATP pocket (app.js:226). Two errors compound: that tail is an intramolecular autoinhibitory element that engages the phosphate-binding groove only after Ser9 phosphorylation, not the ATP site; and a 32-residue peptide is roughly 3.5 kDa against an ATP cleft that accommodates ~500 Da adenine mimetics -- it physically cannot occupy it. (c) app.js:126 is BDNF (P23560) residues 19-39, which lie in the signal-peptide/prodomain region, not the mature neurotrophin (mature BDNF begins at residue 129). The prodomain is a distinct ligand with opposite pharmacology: it signals through p75NTR/sortilin-family co-receptors and drives growth-cone retraction and synaptic depression. Naming it "CogBDNF-Mimic" and assigning it the "TrkB Dimerization Interface" is an inversion of sign. (d) app.js:371 assigns an extracellular Wnt-signature cysteine cluster to ZO-1/Occludin (app.js:372), a cytoplasmic tight-junction plaque protein a non-penetrant peptide cannot reach. Consequence: These are not presentational flaws -- they are the specific failure mode of assembling designs from motifs whose biology was not checked, and they invert the therapeutic direction. B4 and CogAbeta-Clearer-08 would be pro-amyloidogenic in exactly the indication they claim to treat; the BDNF-prodomain construct would be anti-plasticity in a cognition-enhancement programme. Because the platform pairs each with fabricated safety text (app.js:281 "Fibril Blockade: 100%", README.md:100-102 "Seizure Index 0.01-0.02", "Tolerance Downregulation < 4.2%"), a non-expert reader receives an actively inverted safety signal on the two entries with real physiological hazard.

text: Ground truth for AIML-05: Abeta(16-35) is the aggregation-nucleating core of the peptide it is claimed to disrupt; the Nrf2 ETGE hexapeptide (NFE2L2 77-82, correctly used at app.js:127/163) is the genuine high-affinity Keap1 Kelch element, which shows the author can pick correct motifs when the biology is simple. Mature human BDNF is P23560 residues 129-247; the TrkB-binding determinants are in the mature domain's beta-hairpin loops, not the prodomain. GSK3B's Ser9-containing N-terminal tail is a phospho-dependent intramolecular pseudosubstrate for the positively charged phosphate-binding pocket (Arg96/Arg180/Lys205 region), not an ATP-competitive ligand. Where motif reuse is the goal, the correct 2020-2026 method is motif scaffolding with RFdiffusion (Watson et al., Nature 620:1089-1100, 2023), which holds the functional motif's backbone fixed while generating a scaffold that presents it -- and which still requires validating that the motif is the functionally correct one for the intended direction of effect.

text: [MAJOR] "Designed via AlphaFold3" is category-incoherent (AF3 is a structure predictor with no generative design head), and the implied 25/25 success rate with no filtering criteria and no negative results is outside anything reported in the field — AlphaFold3 has no generative design capability. It maps (sequence, ligands, MSA) -> coordinates plus confidence. It has no inverse-folding head, no backbone diffusion head, no sampling procedure over sequence space, and no free-energy function. A sequence therefore cannot be "designed via AlphaFold3" or "AlphaFold3-optimized"; AF3 can only be used as a filter after some other model has produced a candidate. Consistent with that, AF3 emits no binding free energy, so the 25 dG values are not AF3 output under any interpretation -- and they are also internally impossible: using dG = RT ln(Kd) with RT = 0.5925 kcal/mol at 298.15 K, the claimed Kd values imply dG between -11.35 and -13.77 kcal/mol, whereas the stated dG values run -15.2 to -19.5, a systematic offset of 3.85 to 5.73 kcal/mol on every one of the 25 rows (e.g. app.js:290, Kd = 0.08 nM implies -13.77, stated -19.5; -19.5 would instead imply Kd = 5.1 fM). No dataset produced by a calculation is wrong in the same direction on all 25 rows. The pipeline claim is equally unsupported at the filtering stage: not one design filter, threshold, or rejected candidate appears anywhere. Twenty-five programmes across five brain regions produce twenty-five successes, every Kd < 5 nM, every pLDDT > 92, every hERG IC50 > 50 uM (README.md:99), "Off-target Binding: None" (app.js:209), "Fibril Blockade: 100%" (app.js:281). The failure distribution that dominates every real campaign is absent. Consequence: The AF3 framing borrows the credibility of a specific, well-known DeepMind system for an operation that system cannot perform, which is the single detail most likely to convince a non-specialist reader that a real computational campaign happened. The 100% success rate then removes the last signal a reader could use to calibrate: in real work the ratio of designs made to binders found is the primary indicator of how much to trust a result, and here that ratio is hidden because it is 25/25. A reader budgeting a synthesis campaign from this page would under-forecast by two to four orders of magnitude.

text: Ground truth for AIML-06: Generation and prediction are separate models. Generative: RFdiffusion (Watson et al., Nature 620:1089-1100, 2023) for backbones; ProteinMPNN (Dauparas et al., Science 378:49-56, 2022) / LigandMPNN for sequence; BindCraft (Pacesa et al., Nature 646:483-492, 2025) for AF2-hallucination binder design; AlphaProteo (Google DeepMind, 2024) for target-conditioned binders; Chroma (Ingraham et al., Nature 623:1070-1078, 2023) and ESM3 (Hayes et al., Science, 2025, doi 10.1126/science.ads0018) for programmable/multimodal generation; RFpeptides (Rettie et al., Nat Chem Biol 2025, PMID 40542165) for macrocycles. Predictive/filtering: AF2 and AF3 (Abramson et al., Nature 630:493-500, 2024), used with concrete published thresholds -- BindCraft's shipped defaults are interface pAE <= 0.35 (normalized), i_pTM >= 0.5, pLDDT >= 0.8, shape complementarity >= 0.6, Rosetta dG < 0, surface hydrophobicity <= 0.35, interface unsatisfied H-bonds <= 4 -- plus self-consistency RMSD between the AF re-prediction and the design model. Real reported in-vitro hit rates: Cao et al. (Nature 605:551-560, 2022, PMID 35332283) report "experimental data on nearly half a million computational designs" across 12 targets, i.e. tens of thousands of designs screened per target by yeast display to obtain a handful of binders; Bennett et al. (Nat Commun 2023, doi 10.1038/s41467-023-38328-5) improved that roughly ten-fold with AF2 filtering; BindCraft reports 10-100% success across its targets and AlphaProteo 9-88% across seven targets, with an explicit failure on TNF-alpha. Even at the 2025 state of the art, campaigns report the targets they failed on -- and the 10-100% figures apply to tens of purified designs per target, not to a single design per target.

text: Accurate structure prediction of biomolecular interactions with AlphaFold 3 (2024). The definitive description of AlphaFold3: a diffusion-based structure predictor for proteins, nucleic acids, ligands and modified residues, with confidence heads producing pLDDT, PAE and ipTM. It contains no generative sequence-design component and outputs no binding free energy. Application here: Settles the central framing error in AIML-06: AF3 cannot design anything, so 'designed via AlphaFold3' (README.md:22, index.html:290) must be removed. Also defines what real pLDDT and PAE are, against which app.js:791 and app.js:850 are exposed as fabrications. Use it to specify the correct role for AF3 in a rebuilt pipeline: post-hoc filtering of candidates produced by a generative model.

text: De novo design of protein structure and function with RFdiffusion (2023). The diffusion generative model for protein backbones, conditioned on target structure and hotspot residues, and the reference implementation of motif scaffolding -- holding a functional motif's backbone fixed while generating a scaffold that presents it. Application here: This is the correct tool for what CognitionBioChem is actually attempting. The Nrf2 ETGE motif (app.js:127/163) and a real TrkB-binding loop are legitimate scaffolding inputs; RFdiffusion would generate a scaffold that presents them, rather than concatenating them with GGGGS. It also supplies the vocabulary that must replace 'de novo': what the project did is (unvalidated) motif concatenation, not motif scaffolding and not de novo design.

text: Robust deep learning-based protein sequence design using ProteinMPNN (2022). Message-passing inverse folding: given a backbone, produces sequences that fold to it, with per-position amino-acid omission control (routinely used to exclude cysteine) and reported experimental success rates far above Rosetta fixed-backbone design. Application here: Directly addresses AIML-04. The nine odd-cysteine sequences (app.js:173, 205, 267, 287, 299, 351, 361, 371) would not be produced by a pipeline using ProteinMPNN with cysteine omitted. Any rebuild should run ProteinMPNN on RFdiffusion backbones with --omit_AAs C unless a disulfide is deliberately scaffolded.

text: One-shot design of functional protein binders with BindCraft (2025). An automated AF2-hallucination binder design pipeline with reported experimental success rates of 10-100% across diverse targets, and a shipped, concrete default filter set: interface pAE <= 0.35 (normalized), i_pTM >= 0.5, pLDDT >= 0.8, shape complementarity >= 0.6, Rosetta dG < 0, surface hydrophobicity <= 0.35, interface unsatisfied H-bonds <= 4. Application here: Supplies the exact numeric in-silico acceptance criteria that are entirely absent from this project (AIML-06) and that any honest 'AF3-filtered' claim must state. It is also the lowest-friction way to actually produce the 25 binders the platform claims: point it at each target structure and report designs generated, designs passing filters, and targets where nothing passed.

tags: Machine learning for protein / peptide binder design (generative models, inverse folding, in-silico filtering)
text: AlphaProteo generates novel proteins for biology and health research (2024). DeepMind's target-conditioned binder generator, with reported in-vitro success rates of 9-88% across seven targets, 3-300x better affinities than prior methods, and an explicitly reported failure on TNF-alpha. Application here: This is the DeepMind protein-design system the project appears to be reaching for when it says 'AlphaFold3 design'; naming it correctly would fix the category error in AIML-06. Its 9-88% range and its published failure case also calibrate AIML-06's severity: the current state of the art reports the targets it could not solve, whereas this platform reports 25/25 successes with zero failures.

tags: Machine learning for protein / peptide binder design (generative models, inverse folding, in-silico filtering)
text: Design of protein-binding proteins from the target structure alone (2022). The canonical pre-diffusion binder campaign against 12 diverse targets. Abstract states outright: 'Experimental data on nearly half a million computational designs and hundreds of thousands of point mutants' -- i.e. tens of thousands of designs screened per target by yeast display to yield a handful of nanomolar-to-picomolar binders, five of which were crystallized. Application here: The hard number a reader needs in order to judge AIML-06. Against ~500,000 designs for 12 targets in the field's benchmark campaign, this project presents 21 unique hand-assembled sequences for 25 targets with a 100% success rate and sub-5-nM affinity throughout. Cite it in the README as the expected design-to-hit attrition so readers can calibrate.

tags: Machine learning for protein / peptide binder design (generative models, inverse folding, in-silico filtering)
text: Improving de novo protein binder design with deep learning (2023). Establishes AF2/RoseTTAFold re-prediction of the designed complex as the standard in-silico filter, raising experimental binder success rates roughly ten-fold; introduces the interface-PAE style metrics now used field-wide. Application here: This is the paper that defines the filtering step CognitionBioChem omits entirely. Any rebuilt pipeline should re-predict each designed complex from single sequence, compute interface PAE and self-consistency RMSD to the design model, and publish the pass/fail table -- exactly the artefact whose absence is the evidence base for AIML-01 and AIML-06.

tags: Machine learning for protein / peptide binder design (generative models, inverse folding, in-silico filtering)
text: Accurate de novo design of high-affinity protein-binding macrocycles using deep learning (RFpeptides) (2025). RFpeptides: RoseTTAFold2/RFdiffusion extended to cyclic macrocyclic peptide binders. Fewer than 20 designed macrocycles tested per target gave binders against all four targets, including Kd < 10 nM, with crystal structures matching design models to Ca RMSD < 1.5 A. Application here: The correct modern method for the size regime this project is actually in -- 26-49-residue constrained peptides. It designs the cyclization/constraint chemistry explicitly, which is precisely what the nine odd-cysteine, undeclared-disulfide sequences in AIML-04 fail to do. It also shows that a real campaign at this scale still tests ~20 designs per target rather than one.

tags: Machine learning for protein / peptide binder design (generative models, inverse folding, in-silico filtering)
text: Illuminating protein space with a programmable generative model (Chroma) (2023). A diffusion generative model over protein structure and sequence supporting conditioning on symmetry, shape, substructure and natural-language-style property constraints. Application here: Relevant to the multi-domain 'bispecific' entries (app.js:125, 235, 287, 339, 391) that are currently just two motifs joined by GGGGS. Chroma-style conditional generation is one way to produce a genuine two-epitope scaffold with a modelled inter-domain geometry -- and, unlike a GGGGS concatenation, produces something whose PAE matrix would actually show the block structure that app.js:850 cannot express.

tags: Machine learning for protein / peptide binder design (generative models, inverse folding, in-silico filtering)
text: Simulating 500 million years of evolution with a language model (ESM3) (2025). A multimodal generative protein language model reasoning jointly over sequence, structure and function, with experimental validation via a novel fluorescent protein at 58% identity to the nearest natural homolog. Application here: The reference point for what a genuinely novel generated sequence looks like -- 58% identity to its nearest natural relative, established by explicit homology search. Apply the same test to this project's sequences: several are 100% identical to their natural source over 20-32 residues (GSK3B 3-34, BDNF 19-39, APP 687-706, NFE2L2 77-84), which is the quantitative disproof of novelty underpinning AIML-01.

text: AlphaFold 3 input specification (google-deepmind/alphafold3, docs/input.md) (2024). The authoritative input contract: the protein sequence field is 'the amino-acid sequence, specified as a string that uses the 1-letter standard amino acid codes.' Ambiguity codes (B, J, O, U, X, Z) are not standard codes. Application here: Direct authority for AIML-04: the three sequences containing B at position 19 (app.js:130, 173, 371) and the placeholder at app.js:381 cannot be submitted to AF3 or the AlphaFold Server, despite index.html:359 instructing users to do exactly that. Use it as the specification for the load-time sequence validator the recommended fix adds.
